_comment: Packs for the o / a trainer (/articles), see src/lib/artikelPacks.js. `topics` groups the lexicon's own unit topics (src/content/lexicon/*.json; the topic ids stayed German) into everyday packs; a noun belongs to the pack of its FIRST topic, so every tagged noun is in exactly one. `rules` are gender patterns of European Portuguese, checked in this order on the noun's first word (so -ção/-são come before -ão, and -ão before -o); a noun joins a rule pack only if it matches the pattern AND its real article is the pack's article. The ones that match and break it are the exceptions (o dia, a mão, o coração). `names` is a word list, `suffixes` are endings (the code still knows `genusF`, the Spanish el agua case; Portuguese has none). `min` lowers minPack for a rule with few nouns. `noRule` lists set phrases no ending rule speaks about; acronyms (IVA, NIF) are skipped by the code.
_levels: A topic pack's `levels` renames it per level: one lexicon topic holds different nouns at each level (A1 wohnen = kitchen, bathroom; A2 = deposit, landlord), so no pack name repeats across A1–B2. `name`/`icon` are the fallback.

rules.name: -ma words from Greek
rules.rule: Many words in -ma come from Greek and are masculine: o problema, o tema, o sistema, o programa. Not every word in -ma: a cama, a forma, a semana.
rules.ruleLeicht: These words end in -ma, but they take “o”: o problema, o tema.

rules.name: -ção and -são
rules.rule: Nouns in -ção and -são are feminine: a estação, a informação, a televisão, a decisão. The one to watch: o coração.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -ção or -são? Then you say “a”: a estação.

rules.name: -dade and -tude
rules.rule: Nouns in -dade and -tude are feminine: a cidade, a universidade, a liberdade, a juventude, a atitude.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -dade or -tude? Then you say “a”: a cidade.

rules.name: -gem
rules.rule: Nouns in -gem are feminine: a viagem, a mensagem, a garagem, a paisagem, a imagem. Spanish speakers, careful: el viaje, but a viagem.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -gem? Then you say “a”: a viagem.

rules.name: -ise
rules.rule: Nouns in -ise are feminine: a crise, a análise, a tese.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -ise? Then you say “a”: a crise.

rules.name: -ume
rules.rule: Nouns in -ume are masculine: o costume, o legume, o volume, o perfume. Spanish speakers, careful: la costumbre, but o costume.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -ume? Then you say “o”: o costume.

rules.name: -or
rules.rule: Most nouns in -or are masculine: o computador, o motor, o condutor, o elevador. The ones to watch: a flor, a cor, a dor.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -or? Then you usually say “o”: o motor.

rules.name: -ão
rules.rule: Most nouns in -ão (other than -ção and -são) are masculine: o pão, o cão, o avião, o irmão. The ones to watch: a mão, a razão, a opinião, a região.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -ão? Then you usually say “o”: o pão.

rules.name: -o
rules.rule: Most nouns in -o are masculine: o livro, o trabalho, o copo. The ones to watch: a foto, a moto, a tribo.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -o? Then you usually say “o”: o livro.

rules.name: -a
rules.rule: Most nouns in -a are feminine: a casa, a cadeira, a mesa. The ones to watch: o dia, o mapa, o planeta.
rules.ruleLeicht: The word ends in -a? Then you usually say “a”: a casa.
